ci.read: GitHub check runs at the code head: every lane completed, none failed (lint, typecheck, test, build, changes, dispatch, dispatch-memory, dispatch-multiprocess, dispatch-browser-multiprocess, envoy-go, envoy-go-race, envoy-e2e-local, envoy-infra-go, envoy-session-stall, envoy-smoke, pr-title success; the release and package lanes skipped). The pull request head dd557fd9 is the handoff-only push carrying 'skip-checks: true', so GitHub started no run for it and the code head's verdict is the one that counts.

findings: Not this change's, reported to the tree's architect: Go's Parse reads a CommonMark HTML declaration ('<!' then a letter, then anything, then '>') as plain text, while the browser engine reads it as inline HTML. 'p <!a> q' is stored as 'p \<!a> q' and drawn as that text in a document, while a comment holding the same line draws the declaration as raw HTML. Go agrees with the engine on '<b>', '<!-- c -->', '<?x?>' and '<![CDATA[x]]>'; only the declaration kind diverges. Merged main b93381d3 and this head render the three documents a 3,000-document fuzz found byte for byte the same, so the branch neither causes nor fixes it. It is the family dispatch://INFRA-752 covers for addresses followed by '<b>', and no open issue names the declaration shape.
